what: CVS Health is three businesses in one: about 9,000 retail pharmacies, Caremark, one of the largest pharmacy benefit managers, and Aetna, a large health insurer. Money, medicines and patients move between the three.
customers: Consumers filling prescriptions, employers and health plans buying pharmacy benefits, and members of Aetna health plans.
money: negotiating drug prices and processing claims for health plans and employers
medical, Medicare and dental insurance premiums
moat: Scale in drug purchasing that smaller benefit managers cannot match, combined with an insurer and a pharmacy chain that direct patients to each other.
risks: Medicare Advantage medical costs rose faster than premiums and hurt profits badly
Politicians in both US parties have targeted pharmacy benefit managers
Retail pharmacy foot traffic is declining and stores are being closed
Debt of about $75 billion limits flexibility
opportunities: Repricing Medicare Advantage plans can restore insurance margins over two or three years
Owning the insurer, the benefit manager and the pharmacy allows cost control rivals cannot copy
The shares trade at a low multiple of earnings compared with health insurers generally
watch: The Aetna medical benefit ratio, which shows how much of each premium dollar goes out in claims.
